node.title: Re: Any security holes?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I was wondering if there are any security concerns in my .pl file?

Yes - as [LanX] already alluded to, this is susceptible to a [https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/xss/|Cross Site Scripting (XSS)] attack. One way to help mitigate this is to escape any strings you're inserting into the HTML, for example with [mod://HTML::Entities]. Other comments:

  • Always [id://111088]!
  • The whole @pairs code seems unneccessary, it looks like you've copied some really old Perl form parsing code from somewhere, but this is not needed because you're already using [mod://CGI].pm which does this for you.
  • You're not checking [doc://open] for errors - [id://11102684]
  • You're not locking your drivers.html file while you are editing it, which could cause problems when multiple requests are submitted at the same time (though I don't know how [doc://flock] behaves on Windows).

But really, you shouldn't be using this really old-school [mod://CGI].pm style code anymore. You probably want to look into [id://1182902], in particular I'm a fan of [mod://Mojolicious], its templating engine would be very useful here because it can escape HTML special characters automatically when inserting variables into HTML. I have a bunch of Mojo examples [id://830550|on my scratchpad] Update: and I've now posted a full example [id://11145133|here].
